title: Transpose of the finite scalar comparison on the integral duality formula
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\pi,v$, and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $A_n=R/\pi^n$, $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, where $e$ is the ramification index. Work on fixed small pro-etale skeletons with completed coefficient sheaves $\widehat R_W,\widehat S_W$ and bounded derived-complete constructible categories $\mathcal C_R(W),\mathcal C_S(W)$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $T_W=-\widehat\otimes_R^L S$ be the prescribed strict-tower scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $T_{W,n}=-\otimes_{A_n}^LB_n$. Use the constructible adjunctions $F_R=Rf_{!,R}\dashv G_R=Rf_R^!$ and $F_S\dashv G_S$, with units $\eta_R,\eta_S$ and counits $\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_S$, as realized by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. Fix one compactification of $f$ for these functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $\alpha:T_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_ST_X$ be the compact-support scalar comparison obtained by total inverse limit of the finite-free comparisons $\alpha_n:T_{Y,n}F_{A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{B_n}T_{X,n}$: on a basis of the finite free $R$-module $S$ they are finite-sum distributivity. Use the canonical completed-scalar comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] when commuting $T$ with total limit. Write $D_{W,R}K=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_W}(K,\omega_{W,R})$, and similarly over $S$, with the specified dualizing objects and evaluation [thm-coef-integral-verdier]. Let $\kappa_R:G_R\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,R}f_R^*D_{Y,R}$ and $\kappa_S:G_S\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,S}f_S^*D_{Y,S}$ be the canonical integral formula identifications of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]; $f^*$ here is completed pullback. Let $\beta^W_Z:T_WD_{W,R}Z\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{W,S}T_WZ$ be the evaluation-defined comparison of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension], and let $c_Z:T_Xf_R^*Z\xrightarrow{\sim}f_S^*T_YZ$ be the tensor-reassociation pullback comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. For every $M\in\mathcal C_R(Y)$ define
$$d_M=D_{X,S}\bigl(c_{D_{Y,R}M}^{-1}\circ f_S^*((\beta^Y_M)^{-1})\bigr)\circ\beta^X_{f_R^*D_{Y,R}M},$$
$$b'_M=\kappa_{S,T_YM}^{-1}\circ d_M\circ T_X(\kappa_{R,M}):T_XG_RM\longrightarrow G_ST_YM.$$
Then the specified exceptional counit satisfies
$$\varepsilon_{S,T_YM}\circ F_S(b'_M)=T_Y(\varepsilon_{R,M})\circ\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}.$$
The equation uses the canonical evaluation-defined comparisons, including the dualizing comparison adjoint to the scalar-extended structure-morphism counit, and the canonical formula identifications, not arbitrary isomorphisms between the same functors.

proof.text: First work simultaneously at $A=A_n$ and $B=B_n=A_{L,en}$. Write $T=-\otimes_A^LB$, $F_C=Rf_{!,C}$, $G_C=Rf_C^!$, $Q_C=f_C^*D_{Y,C}M$ and $H_CM=D_{X,C}Q_C$ for $C=A,B$ (with $M$ replaced by $T_YM$ over $B$). The finite-free extension lemma gives these coefficient rings and the evaluation-defined finite comparisons. The finite exceptional and biduality theorems put $G_C,D_{W,C}$ in the finite-Tor constructible categories, and pullback preserves them. Tensor products occurring below are also in that domain: constructible cohomology is the finite-tensor theorem, while tensoring flat models supported in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ gives a flat model supported in $[a+c,b+d]$. The structure morphisms $a_W:W\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ are separated finite type as well. Thus all absolute exceptional adjunctions used below are the constructible ones, including for an empty scheme. Choose a finite integer dimension bound for $X$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] (bound zero if $X$ is empty). Ordinary adjunction is clause (1) of [fix-prop-adjunctions], and [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] ensures that its right adjoint preserves the finite-Tor subcategory, as required when using the absolute-trace exchange lemma. Bounded constructible inputs have etale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so the stated domain of compact-support composition is met. The evaluation bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(W,D_{T,C}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(W\otimes N,\omega_{T,C})$, $v\mapsto\operatorname{ev}_N\circ(v\otimes1)$, required by the absolute-trace exchange lemma and used for every currying below, is the internal tensor--Hom isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] followed by $H^0$ and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]; the evaluation and double-dual maps are those of [lem-weil-duality-pairing].

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: finite-level domains and coefficient indices

proof.text:
Put $P_{W,C}=Ra_{W!,C}$ and let $\operatorname{tr}_{W,C}:P_{W,C}\omega_{W,C}\to C_s$ be its counit. Write $\gamma_C:P_{Y,C}F_C\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{X,C}$ for compact-support composition and $\theta_C:F_CK\otimes D_{Y,C}M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_C(K\otimes f_C^*D_{Y,C}M)$ for projection. For $h:K\to H_CM$, put $e_C(h)=\operatorname{ev}_{Q_C}\circ(h\otimes1):K\otimes Q_C\to\omega_{X,C}$. Define $y_C(h):F_CK\otimes D_{Y,C}M\to\omega_{Y,C}$ by the absolute adjunction equation
$$\operatorname{tr}_{Y,C}\circ P_{Y,C}y_C(h)=\operatorname{tr}_{X,C}\circ P_{X,C}e_C(h)\circ\gamma_{C,K\otimes Q_C}\circ P_{Y,C}\theta_C.$$
All factors are specified: composition is [thm-sf-comp-composition], projection is [fix-prop-projection-formula], and the absolute adjunctions and dualizing objects are in [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. This defines a unique $y_C(h)$, not a choice between isomorphic objects.

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: write the absolute trace transpose of evaluation

proof.text:
Use the evaluation bijection in [lem-sf-absolute-trace-exchange] with $P_W=P_{W,C}$ and coefficient object $C_s$. Its displayed Hom action, followed by the evaluation-defined biduality of [thm-fix-general-biduality], gives the bijection
$$\Psi_C(h)=\delta_M^{-1}\circ\operatorname{curry}(y_C(h)):\ F_CK\longrightarrow M.$$
Here currying uses $\operatorname{Hom}(F_CK\otimes D_YM,\omega_Y)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_CK,D_YD_YM)$. To compare this with the finite formula identification, expand the source's four Hom arrows: transpose $h$ by tensor symmetry, use $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, apply the exchange with exactly the trace pairing of the cited absolute-trace lemma, and transpose back by $\delta_M$. The middle two arrows have the Hom action specified by that lemma; the two outside arrows exchange the tensor factors twice. Naturality of symmetry cancels these two exchanges. Their remaining evaluation transpose is precisely the equation defining $y_C(h)$ in Step 2. Thus, writing $\kappa_C:G_C\xrightarrow{\sim}H_C$ for the canonical finite identification, its adjunction normalization is
$$\Psi_C(\kappa_{C,M}\circ z)=\varepsilon_{C,M}\circ F_C(z)\qquad(z:K\to G_CM).$$
The finite diagram-realization statement specifies this same tensor-Hom evaluation transpose, including its counit normalization, on coefficient systems.

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: identify the specified finite formula via its Hom action

proof.text:
For a structure morphism set $\alpha_W:T_sP_{W,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{W,B}T_W$ and $u_W:T_W\omega_{W,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{W,B}$. The explicit normalization in [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] says
$$\operatorname{tr}_{W,B}\circ P_{W,B}(u_W)\circ\alpha_{W,\omega_{W,A}}=T_s(\operatorname{tr}_{W,A}).\tag{1}$$
Apply [lem-coef-finite-free-compact-composition] to $(g,f)=(a_Y,f)$, with $a_Yf=a_X$. It gives the precise composition square needed here:
$$\gamma_B\circ P_{Y,B}(\alpha_f)\circ\alpha_Y=\alpha_X\circ T_s(\gamma_A).\tag{2}$$
Thus the trace calculation uses compatibility of compact-support composition for finite-free scalar extension. The quotient-only statement [lem-sf-compact-coefficient-composition] would not justify this application; no such specialization is made.

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: absolute counit and compact-support composition squares

proof.text:
Let $\beta^W$ be the finite evaluation-defined duality maps and $c$ the tensor-reassociation pullback comparison. Put
$$q_M=f_B^*(\beta^Y_M)\circ c_{D_{Y,A}M}:T_XQ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_B,$$
$$d^n_M=D_{X,B}(q_M^{-1})\circ\beta^X_{Q_A}:T_XH_AM\xrightarrow{\sim}H_BT_YM.$$
The inverse in the first formula of the question is exactly $q_M^{-1}=c^{-1}\circ f_B^*((\beta^Y_M)^{-1})$. Evaluation compatibility in [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] and naturality of evaluation in its first input give, for every $h:K\to H_AM$,
$$e_B(d^n_M\circ T_Xh)\circ(1\otimes q_M)=u_X\circ T_X(e_A(h)).\tag{3}$$
Tensor comparisons are inserted on the right. Explicitly, evaluation after $D(q_M^{-1})$ precomposes its second argument by $q_M^{-1}$; substituting $q_M$ cancels it. Evaluation after $\beta^X$ is $u_X$ times extended old evaluation. This proves (3) with the required contravariant orientation.

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: compare the uncurried dual-formula maps

proof.text:
Abbreviate $y_A=y_A(h)$ and $y_B=y_B(d^n_MT_Xh)$. Let
$$r=\alpha_{f,K}^{-1}\otimes(\beta^Y_M)^{-1}:F_BT_XK\otimes D_{Y,B}T_YM\longrightarrow T_Y(F_AK\otimes D_{Y,A}M)$$
using the scalar tensor isomorphism. The scalar-extension compatibility of projection in [fix-prop-projection-formula] is exactly
$$\theta_B\circ(\alpha_{f,K}\otimes\beta^Y_M)=F_B(1\otimes q_M)\circ\alpha_{f,K\otimes Q_A}\circ T_Y\theta_A.$$
Substitute this and (3) in the defining trace expression for $y_B$. Naturality of $\alpha_f$, followed by (2) and then (1) for $X$, identifies the resulting transpose under $P_{Y,B}\dashv G_{a_Y,B}$ with the scalar extension of the old trace expression. On the other hand (1) for $Y$ and naturality of $\alpha_Y$ give the same transpose for $u_Y\circ T_Yy_A\circ r$. Written on the common source before applying $P_{Y,B}r$, both are
$$T_s\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{X,A}\circ P_{X,A}e_A(h)\circ\gamma_A\circ P_{Y,A}\theta_A\bigr).$$
Precomposition by the invertible $\alpha_Y$ is harmless; injectivity of the absolute adjunction therefore proves
$$y_B=u_Y\circ T_Yy_A\circ r.\tag{4}$$

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: compare both trace transposes and cancel the absolute adjunction

proof.text:
For $g=\Psi_A(h)$, Step 3 and the defining double-dual pairing say
$$y_A(h)=\operatorname{ev}_{M,A}\circ\sigma\circ(g\otimes1_{D_{Y,A}M}).$$
Indeed uncurrying $\delta_M\circ g$ is evaluation with these factors reversed. Apply $T_Y$, then $u_Y$, and substitute (4). Evaluation preservation by $\beta^Y_M$ turns this into
$$y_B(d^n_MT_Xh)=\operatorname{ev}_{T_YM,B}\circ\sigma\circ((T_Yg\circ\alpha_{f,K}^{-1})\otimes1).$$
There is no extra scalar or symmetry factor: the tensor reassociation acts on elementary tensors by multiplying the two coefficient scalars, and the two symmetries have the same Koszul sign. Currying and cancelling the isomorphism $\delta_{T_YM}$ now yield
$$\Psi_B(d^n_M\circ T_Xh)=T_Y(\Psi_A(h))\circ\alpha_{f,K}^{-1}.\tag{5}$$

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: finish the finite Hom-bijection square by evaluation

proof.text:
Take $K=G_AM$ and $h=\kappa_{A,M}$. Step 3 gives $\Psi_A(h)=\varepsilon_{A,M}$. Set
$$b'_{n,M}=\kappa_{B,T_YM}^{-1}\circ d^n_M\circ T_X(\kappa_{A,M}).$$
The same normalization over $B$ and (5) give
$$\varepsilon_{B,T_YM}\circ F_B(b'_{n,M})=T_Y(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ\alpha_{f,G_AM}^{-1}.\tag{6}$$
Consequently $b'_{n,M}$ is the finite exceptional transpose specified in [lem-coef-finite-scalar-mate-realization]: both have the right side of (6) as their transpose, and an adjunction bijection is injective. This is a calculation of the dual-formula comparison, not an inference that all isomorphisms between these functors coincide.

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: identify the finite comparison with the finite exceptional mate

proof.text: Perform Steps 2-8 on the simultaneous derived coefficient-system models. The finite adjunction-diagram realization supplies $\mathcal F_f,\mathcal E_f$, the duality formula and the actual mapping-system adjunction, also for $a_X,a_Y$. The semilinear-section theorem supplies simultaneous tensor, coefficient extension, ordinary adjunction and composition models, and says evaluation, composition and taking transposes preserve their coherence homotopies. Its first-input condition for internal Hom is satisfied: the reduction systems of $M$, its dual and $f^*D_YM$ are cartesian, by their normalized quotient comparisons in the finite exceptional diagram realization. The evaluation calculus makes the relevant equalities evaluation/transpose identities of system maps. Thus the proof of (3)-(6) applies to those constructions themselves: cancellation is cancellation of inverse system comparisons, trace adjunction is the specified system adjunction, and (2) is the coherent identity in [lem-coef-finite-free-compact-composition], not a purported consequence of levelwise equality. It follows that the coherent $b'_\bullet$ defined by the dual-formula composite equals the coherent exceptional transpose $b_\bullet$ of [lem-coef-finite-scalar-mate-realization]. We have not deduced equality of system maps from equality of their individual evaluations.

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: retain the equality as an identity of the specified coherent constructions

proof.text:
Now use the integral objects of the question. Set $P=T_XG_RM$ and let $E_\bullet$ be its finite scalar-extended exceptional system; let $N_\bullet$ be the chosen $B_n$-exceptional system with total limit $G_ST_YM$. The coherent integral formula and adjunction are those of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. The integral Verdier comparisons preserve evaluation and its transposes. The integral finite-extension maps $\beta^W$ preserve evaluation and have the finite comparisons specified in [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]; pullback uses the reassociation of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Denote the resulting source comparison by $a:\mathcal R_X^SP\to E_\bullet$, and the reduction/limit counit at $N_\bullet$ by $e_N$. On the simultaneous evaluation models of the calculus, substitution in the formula defining $b'_M$ gives the system identity
$$e_N\circ\mathcal R_X^S(b'_M)=b'_\bullet\circ a.\tag{7}$$
This is substitution in the specified evaluation/transpose constructions: the two contravariant inverses give $q^{-1}$, the outer evaluation gives $\beta^X$, and the two formula comparisons give $\kappa_B^{-1}$ and $T\kappa_A$. It is not inferred by checking only the evaluations of (7).

source.place: blueprint_update.proof paragraph 8, expanded: identify the prescribed integral maps with their coherent realizations

proof.text:
Let $u_P:P\to\mathcal L_X^S\mathcal R_X^SP$ be the reduction/limit adjunction unit. Under that adjunction the system map $b_\bullet a$ corresponds to
$$v=\mathcal L_X^S(b_\bullet a)\circ u_P:P\to\mathcal L_X^SN_\bullet=G_ST_YM.$$
Its adjoint is exactly $b_\bullet a$, by the unit/counit identity; equivalently $e_N\mathcal R_X^S(v)=b_\bullet a$. Step 9 and (7) therefore give $b'_M=v$ by injectivity of this adjunction bijection. This avoids assuming that finite reduction is faithful. The total-limit functor is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and the canonical completed-scalar comparison identifies the source map $\mathcal L_X^S(a)u_P$ with the prescribed source completion map on the cofinal $en$ levels. Thus the total-limit transpose assertion of [lem-coef-finite-scalar-mate-realization] applies to $v$: its $F_S\dashv G_S$ transpose is $T_Y\varepsilon_{R,M}\circ\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}$. Applying the inverse exceptional adjunction bijection to $b'_M=v$ proves the required equation.
